chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I read to you the bequest of Fatima (peace be upon her)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, so he brought out a box or a basket, and extracted a letter from it. So he read it: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), bequeathed. I bequeath her seven walled gardens: Al-Awaf, Al-Dallal, Al-Barqa, Al-Maysab, Al-Husna, Al-Safiya, and what belonged to the mother of Ibrahim, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So if Ali passes away, then to Al-Hasan. So if Al-Hasan passes away, then to Al-Husayn. So if Al-Husayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children.' Allah was a Witness upon that, and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam; and it was written by Ali ibn Abi Talib.
And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Asim ibn Humayd, similar to it, but did not mention a box or a basket, and she said: 'To the eldest of my children besides your children.'
ai.seo_question: What were the specific properties bequeathed by Fatima (peace be upon her) and who was the ultimate heir?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi details the specific bequest of Fatima bint Muhammad (as) regarding her seven properties, establishing a clear line of succession for inheritance through Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and finally the eldest of her offspring. The inclusion of prominent witnesses like Al-Miqdad, Al-Zubayr, and Ali himself underscores the authenticity and public nature of this will, serving as a key textual evidence for the Ahl al-Bayt's property rights and the principle of inheritance within the Imamate lineage.
